Independent confirmation: (1) Pennsylvania DEP's own Pipeline Portal page (state regulator, names 'Revolution Pipeline', operator 'ETC Northeast Pipeline, LLC', counties Allegheny/Beaver/Butler/Washington, and the 2018-2021 compliance-order timeline), (2) Wikipedia (40.5-mile, 24-inch, same four counties, Sept. 10, 2018 explosion, Energy Transfer Partners), (3) Natural Gas Intelligence 2021-03-03 restart article (independent trade press: names the line, 'the natural gas gathering Revolution Pipeline', operator 'ETC Northeast Pipeline LLC', capacity and endpoint detail), (4) Pittsburgh Post-Gazette 2021-03-01 (independent newspaper, '40.5-mile project designed to ferry gas from fracked shale wells through Butler, Beaver, Allegheny and Washington counties'), (5) DeSmog 2018-09-12 ('The 24-inch diameter pipeline responsible for the blast had gone into service just seven days earlier'), (6) Marcellus Drilling News, referencing its own June 2015 coverage of ETP's original $1.5B 'Revolution Pipeline/Plant Project' announcement (100-mile GATHERING pipeline SYSTEM + separate cryogenic processing plant). I opened all 8 of the row's harvested gem.wiki citations (Pipeline News PDF -- link now 404s on S3, treated as dead, not deleted from the record since it once supported the row; FracTracker map page; EIA data portal page -- generic, does not name this pipeline, not usable as a ref per the relevance rule; PA DEP page -- used; Yahoo Finance/Zacks explosion syndication -- page loads but article body is not present in the static/archived rendering, could not confirm content, not cited; two Natural Gas Intelligence pieces -- one used (restart), one (2022 criminal-charges piece) opened but not needed for any of this row's cells; The Times/timesonline.com criminal-charges piece -- opened, redundant with the NGI piece, not cited) and searched well beyond the pool (PA DEP, Wikipedia, Post-Gazette, DeSmog, Marcellus Drilling News, Oil & Gas Journal, World Pipelines). CAVEAT: StartYear1=2018 is technically the year the line first went into service (about a week before the Sept. 10, 2018 rupture); it was then offline under DEP order until restart in March 2021. I am not proposing a StartYear2 (recorded convention for this field is unclear for a stop/restart of the same never-decommissioned segment) -- flagging only, not changing.

The current 120.00 mi is materially wrong and disagrees with FOUR independent sources that all name this exact line and its exact endpoints (Butler County -> Bulger/Washington County): Pennsylvania DEP's own Pipeline Portal page ('approximately 40.5 miles'), Wikipedia ('a 40.5-mile (65.2 km) long ... pipeline'), Natural Gas Intelligence's 2021 restart article ('the 40.5-mile pipeline to return to service'), and the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette ('the 40.5-mile project ... through Butler, Beaver, Allegheny and Washington counties'). None of these four cite each other or GEM; PA DEP is a state regulator, the other three are independent editorial/trade outlets. I could not find where 120 mi originated, but I did find a plausible aggregate-vs-segment source of confusion: Energy Transfer's original June 2015 announcement (reported contemporaneously by Oil & Gas Journal, World Pipelines and Marcellus Drilling News) described the *entire* 'Revolution Project' -- pipeline system plus a new cryogenic processing plant -- as involving 'approximately 100 miles of high pressure 24- and 30-inch rich gas pipeline' (a multi-lateral GATHERING SYSTEM, not the single 40.5-mile trunk this GEM row tracks). 120 does not exactly match that 100-mile system figure either, so it may be a separate transcription error, but the direction of the error (segment row inflated toward a system-level or announcement-level figure) matches the pattern this sweep brief flags for Rover/Rockies Express/Eastern Shore.

validity.recommendation: set PipelineType (currently blank) to a gathering-line value rather than treating this as an ordinary transmission trunk
validity.researcher_notes: PipelineType is currently blank on the sheet (not in this batch's worklist scope, so no fills[] object staged for it, but it is a real gap worth flagging under the classification check). Two independent trade-press sources explicitly call this a gathering line: Natural Gas Intelligence's own text reads 'The natural gas gathering Revolution Pipeline in Western Pennsylvania has been cleared to restart service...', and Marcellus Drilling News describes the wider project as 'a 100-mile gathering pipeline system in Butler County, PA (lots of wet gas to move)'. This is also consistent with the line's actual function -- moving unprocessed 'rich' (NGL-laden) shale gas from production fields in Butler County to a cryogenic PROCESSING facility in Washington County (NGI), which is the textbook PHMSA definition of a gathering line (wellhead/production area to a processing plant) rather than a transmission line (processing plant/storage to a distribution system or large end customer). Not calling this existence or duplicate doubt -- the physical pipe is real and this is the right row for it -- but the tracker currently carries it with no PipelineType at all, and the evidence points to 'gathering' rather than leaving it to default to a transmission-style read.
